pages.summary: Days and fractions of a year between dates, by the conventions of financial markets.
body: `daysact` counts the actual days; `days360` counts every month as 30 days and the year as 360 (the 30/360 convention of many bonds); `yearfrac` gives the fraction of a year by a basis: 0 actual/actual (the default), 1 30/360 SIA, 2 actual/360, 3 actual/365, 4 30/360 PSA, 5 30/360 ISDA, 6 30/360 European, 7 actual/365 Japanese, 12 actual/actual ISDA, 13 business days over 252. Dates are serial date numbers, date text or datetimes.

examples.title: Half a year, counted several ways

body: `holidays` gives the New York Stock Exchange's regular holidays as the exchange observes them (a holiday on a weekend moves to the Friday before or the Monday after; closings for special events are not included), as serial date numbers. A business day is neither a weekend day (Saturday and Sunday, unless `Weekend` flags others, 7 flags from Sunday) nor a holiday (those, unless a list is given). `isbusday` tests dates; `busdate` gives the next business day (or the previous, Direction -1); `fbusdate` and `lbusdate` the first and last of a month.

examples.title: The exchange's year
examples.code:
h = holidays(datenum(2026, 1, 1), datenum(2026, 12, 31));
datestr(h, 'ddd dd-mmm')
isbusday(datenum(2026, 7, [2 3 6]))
datestr(busdate(datenum(2026, 7, 2)))
datestr([fbusdate(2026, 1); lbusdate(2026, 5)])

pages.summary: A mean-variance portfolio problem: the assets' expected returns and covariance, and the constraints on the weights.
body: A `Portfolio` holds the assets' means and covariance (given by `setAssetMoments`, or estimated from returns by `estimateAssetMoments`), a risk-free rate, and constraints on the weights: bounds on each (`setBounds`), on their sum (`setBudget`), and linear inequalities and equalities. `setDefaultConstraints` makes it long only and fully invested (weights at least 0, summing to 1). Each function gives a new Portfolio, `p = setBounds(p, ...)`; name-value pairs set the same things at once. The `estimate` functions then find portfolios on the efficient frontier.

examples.title: Four assets, no more than 40% in any, and the last two at most half together

pages.summary: Portfolios on the efficient frontier: the least risk for each return.
body: `estimateFrontier` gives NumPorts portfolios (10 unless given), a column each, equally spaced in return from the least-risk one to the largest-return one; `estimateFrontierLimits` those two ends (or one, `'min'` or `'max'`); `estimateFrontierByReturn` the least-risk portfolio of a target return, `estimateFrontierByRisk` the largest-return one of a target risk; `estimateMaxSharpeRatio` the one whose excess return over the risk-free rate per unit of risk is largest. `plotFrontier` draws the frontier, risk against return.
syntax: The least risk for a return.
The largest return for a risk.

examples.title: The frontier and its best portfolio

body: For weights a column each, the expected return m' w and the risk, the standard deviation sqrt(w' C w), by the portfolio's moments.

examples.title: Equal weights against the frontier's ends

pages.summary: The efficient frontier the older way, and portfolios' risks and returns.
body: `portopt` takes the expected returns and covariance directly: long only and fully invested, with further constraints as rows [A b] of A w <= b. It gives NumPorts portfolios along the frontier (or those of the returns given), their risks and returns, the weights a row each; without outputs it draws the frontier. `portstats` gives the risks and returns of weights given as rows.

pages.summary: The value at risk of a portfolio whose returns are normal.
body: The loss that is exceeded with probability RiskThreshold (0.05 unless given) over the period of the returns: -(PortReturn + norminv(RiskThreshold) PortRisk) PortValue (PortValue 1 unless given), as a positive number for a loss.

pages.summary: A covariance from standard deviations and correlations, and back.
body: `corr2cov` gives C(i, j) = s(i) s(j) R(i, j); `cov2corr` gives the standard deviations (the square roots of the diagonal) and the correlations.
